provinces.name: Ontario
provinces.analysis:
Ontario's unemployment rate stood at 7.5% in April 20261, above the national 6.9%. Ontario Budget 2026 projects the provincial rate easing from 7.7% in 2025 to 7.4% in 20262. The province added 80,900 net jobs in 2025; Budget 2026 anticipates softer 2026 job growth tied to slower population growth from federal immigration changes2.

Ontario CPI was +2.9% year-over-year, the highest among the four largest provinces, while provincial GDP growth registered +1.2%1. Provincial economic accounts (most recent available, Q3 2025) recorded exports of $638,705M (+4.3%) and goods GDP of $177,899M (-1.5%).

Honda indefinitely suspended its $15B Ontario EV and battery investment at Alliston3; the corresponding records are tagged Cancelled and excluded from the active pipeline, so the suspended amount is not counted toward active provincial capital value. The project database tracks 728 Ontario projects with roughly $360B in stated value, led by infrastructure (31 valued projects, ~$123B) including the $27.4B Ontario Line and $26.1B GO Expansion. Ontario Budget 2026 sets a $210B ten-year capital plan linked to 412 tracked projects2. Agnico Eagle's Northeastern Ontario Mining Expansion ($14B) advanced from Proposed to Approved4.
provinces.sectorHighlights: Infrastructure leads Ontario's tracked pipeline with 31 valued projects (~$123B), including the $27.4B Ontario Line and $26.1B GO Expansion. Mining follows with 10 projects (~$80B); Agnico Eagle's Northeastern Ontario Mining Expansion ($14B) advanced to Approved. Power and energy adds 15 projects (~$66B). The indefinitely suspended ~$15B Honda EV investment removes a major manufacturing line from the active outlook.
provinces.labourDeepDive: Ontario unemployment was 7.5% in April 2026, above the national 6.9%. The province added 80,900 net jobs in 2025. Ontario Budget 2026 projects the rate easing from 7.7% (2025) to 7.4% (2026), with softer 2026 job growth tied to slower population growth from federal immigration changes. Participation rate was 64.8% and the employment rate 59.9%.
provinces.consumerPulse: Ontario CPI was +2.9% year-over-year, the highest among the four largest provinces. Provincial GDP growth registered +1.2%. The combination of above-national unemployment (7.5%) and the highest large-province CPI frames consumer conditions; provincial economic accounts (Q3 2025, most recent available) show exports up 4.3% and goods GDP down 1.5%.
provinces.marketContext: Ontario's tracked pipeline spans 728 projects with ~$360B in stated value (Cancelled Honda entries in the raw aggregate). The largest components are infrastructure (31 valued projects, ~$123B), mining (10 projects, ~$80B), and power/energy (15 projects, ~$66B). CAD/USD and steel/copper price moves flow through to the manufacturing pipeline, while the indefinitely suspended ~$15B Honda EV investment removes a major manufacturing line from the active outlook.
provinces.tradeExposure: Ontario provincial accounts (Q3 2025, most recent available) show exports of $638,705M (+4.3%) and imports of $610,076M (+1.2%); goods GDP $177,899M (-1.5%). Exposure runs through manufacturing (auto/steel) and mining.

provinces.name: Quebec
provinces.analysis:
Quebec employment fell 43,300 in April 2026 (-0.9%)1, with cumulative 2026 losses near 87,000 jobs2. About half the losses concentrated in construction and manufacturing and roughly one quarter in financial services; the unemployment rate rose to 6.2%1.

Quebec CPI was -0.4% year-over-year, the lowest among provinces, while provincial GDP growth registered +1.3%. Provincial accounts (most recent available, Q3 2025) recorded real GDP of $486,872.74M (-0.1%) and exports of $208,930M (+0.2%)3.

The construction and manufacturing job losses align with a construction-intensive pipeline. The project database tracks 520 Quebec projects with roughly $78.4B in stated value: power and energy leads with 29 valued projects (~$35.4B), followed by mining (23 projects, ~$19.9B) and infrastructure (17 projects, ~$18.1B) including the Montreal Metro Blue Line extension, TramCite and REM branches. Quebec Budget 2026-27 carries a $167B infrastructure plan linked to 289 tracked projects3. Telesat Lightspeed has invested $1.8B with 600 Quebec jobs4.
provinces.sectorHighlights: Power and energy leads Quebec's tracked pipeline with 29 valued projects (~$35.4B), including the $9.0B Parc eolien zone Chamouchouane Hydro-Quebec wind farm. Mining follows with 23 projects (~$19.9B), and infrastructure adds 17 projects (~$18.1B) covering the $4.9B Blue Line metro extension and the $3.8B Quebec City TramCite. Construction and manufacturing absorbed roughly half the 2026 job losses.
provinces.labourDeepDive: Quebec employment fell 43,300 in April 2026 (-0.9%); cumulative 2026 losses are near 87,000, about half in construction and manufacturing and roughly one quarter in financial services. The unemployment rate rose to 6.2%. Participation rate was 64.4% and the employment rate 60.4%. Weekly earnings were $1,280.65 in February 2026.
provinces.consumerPulse: Quebec CPI was -0.4% year-over-year, the lowest among provinces. Provincial GDP growth registered +1.3%. The negative CPI print accompanies the largest single-month 2026 employment decline among large provinces (-43,300 in April), framing household conditions; Quebec manufacturing sales were $228,889M in March 2026.
provinces.marketContext: Quebec's tracked pipeline spans 520 projects with ~$78.4B in stated value. Largest components are power/energy (29 valued projects, ~$35.4B), mining (23 projects, ~$19.9B), and infrastructure (17 projects, ~$18.1B). Hydro-Quebec wind capacity and lithium mining tie the pipeline to power demand and critical-mineral pricing; CAD/USD moves flow through to the manufacturing base that absorbed part of the 2026 job losses.
provinces.tradeExposure: Quebec provincial accounts (Q3 2025, most recent available) show exports $208,930M (+0.2%) and imports $235,767M (-0.5%); intl exports $86,964M (Feb 2026). Manufacturing and lithium/critical-mineral export exposure dominates.

provinces.name: Alberta
provinces.analysis:
ATB raised Alberta's 2026 real GDP forecast to 2.7% from 2.1% and nominal GDP to +6%, citing higher oil prices and a 2026 WTI forecast near US$75/bbl1; indicators carry provincial GDP growth at +2.7%. Alberta unemployment was 7.0% in April 2026, in line with the national rate, with roughly 85,000 jobs added over the prior year3.

One report states the fiscal position could move from a ~$9.4B deficit to a ~$6B surplus if elevated oil prices are sustained2. Alberta CPI was +1.3% year-over-year. The Canada-Alberta Co-operation Agreement on environmental and impact assessment, signed April 2, 2026, caps assessment timelines at two years4; the Flipi Gas-Fired Generation Project (460 MW, TransAlta) was Approved via IAAC early decision after a 64-day review.

The project database tracks 733 Alberta projects with roughly $346.9B in stated value: power and energy leads with 74 valued projects (~$137.3B), followed by manufacturing (17 projects, ~$65.8B) and oil and gas (16 projects, ~$44.4B). The $50B Olds AI Data Centre Hub is the largest single first-tracked record. WTI and WCS price moves flow through to the Pathways Alliance carbon capture hub ($16.5B) and Dow's net-zero facility ($11.5B).
provinces.sectorHighlights: Power and energy leads Alberta's tracked pipeline with 74 valued projects (~$137.3B), including the $16.5B Pathways Alliance carbon capture hub and the $11.5B Dow net-zero facility. Manufacturing follows with 17 projects (~$65.8B), and oil and gas adds 16 projects (~$44.4B). The $50B Olds AI Data Centre Hub is the largest single first-tracked record this week; Flipi Gas-Fired Generation (460 MW) was Approved via IAAC early decision.
provinces.labourDeepDive: Alberta unemployment was 7.0% in April 2026, in line with the national rate, with roughly 85,000 jobs added over the prior year per the spring economic snapshot. The participation rate was 69.2%, among the highest provincially, and the employment rate 64.4%. ATB lifted the 2026 real GDP forecast to 2.7% on higher oil prices.
provinces.consumerPulse: Alberta CPI was +1.3% year-over-year, below the national rate. Provincial GDP growth registered +2.7% on the ATB upgrade tied to higher oil prices. Strong oil-price forecasts underpin a report stating the fiscal position could shift from a ~$9.4B deficit to a ~$6B surplus if sustained, framing the household and fiscal backdrop.
provinces.marketContext: Alberta's tracked pipeline spans 733 projects with ~$346.9B in stated value. Largest components are power/energy (74 valued projects, ~$137.3B), manufacturing (17 projects, ~$65.8B), and oil_gas (16 projects, ~$44.4B). WTI and WCS price moves flow directly through to the oil_gas and power/energy capital plans (Pathways CCS, AOSP Jackpine, Dow Path2Zero); a $50B Olds AI Data Centre Hub is the largest single first-tracked record.
provinces.tradeExposure: Alberta exposure is dominated by oil and gas: WTI and WCS price moves flow through to 16 oil_gas projects (~$44.4B) and a 74-project power/energy pipeline (~$137.3B). Higher 2026 oil-price forecasts underpin the ATB GDP upgrade.

provinces.name: British Columbia
provinces.analysis:
B.C. unemployment was 6.8% in April 20262, below the national 6.9%. B.C. CPI was +2.0% year-over-year and provincial GDP growth registered +1.2%. B.C. Budget 2026 adds $3M for mineral permitting improvements and introduces fixed timelines for mineral exploration permits, processed in as little as 40 days, described as a Canadian first1; B.C. is Canada's largest copper producer and only molybdenum producer.

The project database tracks 694 B.C. projects with roughly $511.3B in stated value, the largest provincial pipeline value tracked. Power and energy leads with 67 valued projects (~$202.7B), followed by mining (47 projects, ~$70.0B) and oil and gas (11 projects, ~$53.1B). The BC Government 2025 call-for-power response is linked to 137 tracked projects across mining, oil and gas, and power and energy3.

Natural-gas and LNG price moves flow through to LNG Canada Phase 1 ($47.9B) and Ksi Lisims LNG ($10B); copper prices intersect the 47-project mining pipeline. The North Shore Wastewater Treatment Plant moved from Under Construction to Complete. First-tracked records include the TELUS AI Data Centre Expansion ($9B) and the Surrey Langley SkyTrain Extension ($6B)4.
provinces.sectorHighlights: Power and energy leads B.C.'s tracked pipeline with 67 valued projects (~$202.7B), including LNG Canada Phase 1 ($47.9B), the Site C hydro project ($16B), and Ksi Lisims LNG ($10B). Mining follows with 47 projects (~$70.0B); B.C. Budget 2026 introduces fixed 40-day mineral exploration permit timelines. Oil and gas adds 11 projects (~$53.1B). B.C. is Canada's largest copper producer and only molybdenum producer.
provinces.labourDeepDive: B.C. unemployment was 6.8% in April 2026, below the national 6.9%. The participation rate was 64.4% and the employment rate 60.0%. The provincial finance minister issued a statement on the April LFS results. B.C. Budget 2026 pairs labour conditions with faster mineral permitting (fixed 40-day exploration timelines) and the 2025 call-for-power response.
provinces.consumerPulse: B.C. CPI was +2.0% year-over-year, at the national pace, while provincial GDP growth registered +1.2%. Unemployment at 6.8% sits just below the national rate. A short-term rental opt-out acceleration policy links to 51 tracked residential projects, framing the housing and consumer backdrop.
provinces.marketContext: B.C.'s tracked pipeline spans 694 projects with ~$511.3B in stated value, the largest provincial pipeline value tracked. Largest components are power/energy (67 valued projects, ~$202.7B), mining (47 projects, ~$70.0B), and oil_gas (11 projects, ~$53.1B). Natural-gas and LNG price moves flow through to LNG Canada Phase 1 ($47.9B) and Ksi Lisims LNG ($10B); copper prices intersect the 47-project mining pipeline.
provinces.tradeExposure: B.C. exposure runs through LNG and natural gas (LNG Canada Phase 1 $47.9B, Ksi Lisims LNG $10B) and copper mining (47 valued mining projects, ~$70.0B). B.C. is Canada's largest copper producer and only molybdenum producer.

provinces.name: Saskatchewan
provinces.analysis:
Saskatchewan's mining sector generated over $12.8B in mineral sales in 2025 (+19% versus 2024): potash rose 18% to $9.3B and uranium 24% to $3.2B, an industry record1. Mining employs over 20,000 directly and via contractors4.

Saskatchewan unemployment was 5.6% in April 20263, the second-lowest among provinces and below the national 6.9%; the April LFS showed employment -4,000 (-0.6%). Saskatchewan CPI was +2.3% year-over-year and provincial GDP growth registered +3.4%2.

The project database tracks 216 Saskatchewan projects with roughly $30.1B in stated value: mining leads with 11 valued projects (~$20.1B), followed by power and energy (12 projects, ~$6.2B). BHP's Jansen Stage 1 ($7.5B) and Stage 2 ($6.4B) anchor the potash pipeline, and NexGen's Rook I ($1.3B) the uranium pipeline. The Bell AI Fabric 300 MW Data Centre in the RM of Sherwood ($1.7B) was first tracked.
provinces.sectorHighlights: Mining leads Saskatchewan's tracked pipeline with 11 valued projects (~$20.1B), anchored by BHP's Jansen Stage 1 ($7.5B) and Stage 2 ($6.4B) potash mines and NexGen's Rook I uranium project ($1.3B). Power and energy follows with 12 projects (~$6.2B), including the $2.0B FCL renewable diesel plant. 2025 potash sales were $9.3B (+18%) and uranium $3.2B (+24%, a record).
provinces.labourDeepDive: Saskatchewan unemployment was 5.6% in April 2026, the second-lowest among provinces and below the national 6.9%; the April LFS showed employment -4,000 (-0.6%). Participation rate was 67.1% and the employment rate 63.3%. Mining employs over 20,000; resource roles pay 20-40% above equivalents, against an average provincial salary near $65,300.
provinces.consumerPulse: Saskatchewan CPI was +2.3% year-over-year while provincial GDP growth registered +3.4%. Unemployment at 5.6% is the second-lowest among provinces. Record 2025 mineral sales above $12.8B (+19%) and resource-sector wage premiums frame household and spending conditions.
provinces.marketContext: Saskatchewan's tracked pipeline spans 216 projects with ~$30.1B in stated value. Largest components are mining (11 valued projects, ~$20.1B) and power/energy (12 projects, ~$6.2B). Potash and uranium prices flow directly through to the mining pipeline (BHP Jansen Stage 1 $7.5B, Stage 2 $6.4B; NexGen Rook I $1.3B uranium); 2025 uranium sales set an industry record at $3.2B.
provinces.tradeExposure: Saskatchewan exposure is concentrated in potash and uranium: 11 valued mining projects (~$20.1B) including BHP Jansen ($7.5B + $6.4B). 2025 potash sales were $9.3B (+18%) and uranium $3.2B (+24%, a record).

provinces.name: Manitoba
provinces.analysis:
Manitoba unemployment was 5.0% in April 20264, the lowest among provinces and below the national 6.9%. Manitoba CPI was +3.3% year-over-year, among the highest provincially, and provincial GDP growth registered +1.1%.

Manitoba Budget 2026 sets the largest-ever capital budget at $3.8B this year, averaging $4.3B per year over five years, and $21.6B in infrastructure over five years, of which $9.5B runs through crown agencies including Manitoba Hydro1. The budget commits to training 40% more apprentices and 4,054 net new health-care staff2, and provides $262.5M for the Arctic Gateway / Port of Churchill plus a $10M Churchill Catalyst Fund.

The project database tracks 2,054 Manitoba projects, the largest provincial count, with roughly $6.7B in stated value reflecting many municipal water and road records. Infrastructure leads with 32 valued projects (~$4.5B), and power and energy adds ~$0.9B via Manitoba Hydro. The record provincial capital plan aligns with the infrastructure pipeline3.
provinces.sectorHighlights: Infrastructure leads Manitoba's tracked pipeline with 32 valued projects (~$4.5B), predominantly municipal water and road work, including the $0.5B North End Sewage Treatment Plant biosolids upgrade and the $0.49B Lake Manitoba/Lake St. Martin outlet channels. Power and energy adds ~$0.9B via Manitoba Hydro, including the $0.39B Pointe du Bois renewable energy project. Manitoba Budget 2026 sets the largest-ever $3.8B capital budget.
provinces.labourDeepDive: Manitoba unemployment was 5.0% in April 2026, the lowest among provinces and below the national 6.9%. Participation rate was 66.5% and the employment rate 63.1%. Budget 2026 commits to training 40% more apprentices and adding 4,054 net new health-care staff, aligned with the largest provincial project count in the database (2,054).
provinces.consumerPulse: Manitoba CPI was +3.3% year-over-year, among the highest provincially, while provincial GDP growth registered +1.1%. Unemployment at 5.0% is the lowest among provinces. The combination of the lowest provincial unemployment and an elevated CPI frames household spending conditions; Budget 2026 funds health-care staffing and apprentice training.
provinces.marketContext: Manitoba's tracked pipeline spans 2,054 projects (the largest provincial count) with ~$6.7B in stated value. The largest component is infrastructure (32 valued projects, ~$4.5B), predominantly municipal water and road work; power/energy adds ~$0.9B (Manitoba Hydro). Most records are smaller municipal projects with limited direct commodity exposure; Manitoba Hydro capital intersects electricity-system planning.
provinces.tradeExposure: Manitoba's pipeline is dominated by municipal infrastructure with limited direct commodity exposure; Manitoba Hydro capital (~$0.9B power/energy) intersects electricity-system planning and the Arctic Gateway / Port of Churchill rail corridor.

provinces.name: Nova Scotia
provinces.analysis:
Nova Scotia unemployment was 6.3% in April 2026, below the national 6.9%. Nova Scotia CPI was +1.7% year-over-year and provincial GDP growth registered +2.7%.

Nova Scotia is advancing offshore wind with a first call for bids in 2026 for up to 5 GW and subsequent calls for up to 10 GW more1; Premier Houston's Wind West Strategic Plan describes a $60B plan for 5 GW2. The Powering the Economy Act is linked to 45 tracked projects3, and over 50 companies are active in offshore-wind-aligned supply-chain sectors.

The project database tracks 339 Nova Scotia projects with roughly $13B in stated value. Power and energy leads with 8 valued projects (~$8.9B), anchored by the $8B Bear Head Energy project. Offshore wind sits upstream of the pipeline; natural-gas power generation ties capital to electricity and gas markets. The federal Impact Assessment Registry lists 8 NS projects, including the Regional Assessment of Oil and Gas Exploratory Drilling and the Marshdale Natural Gas Power Generation Facility.
provinces.sectorHighlights: Power and energy leads Nova Scotia's tracked pipeline with 8 valued projects (~$8.9B), led by the $8B Bear Head Energy clean-energy/hydrogen project and the $0.35B NSP battery storage program. Offshore wind sits upstream within the Wind West $60B / 5 GW framework, with a first call for up to 5 GW in 2026 and over 50 companies active in supply-chain sectors. Environment adds the $0.37B Boat Harbour remediation.
provinces.labourDeepDive: Nova Scotia unemployment was 6.3% in April 2026, below the national 6.9%. Participation rate was 61.3% and the employment rate 57.4%. Over 50 companies are active in offshore-wind-aligned supply-chain sectors, positioned ahead of the 2026 first call for up to 5 GW under the Wind West framework.
provinces.consumerPulse: Nova Scotia CPI was +1.7% year-over-year, below the national rate, while provincial GDP growth registered +2.7%. Unemployment at 6.3% sits below the national 6.9%. The combination of below-national inflation and below-national unemployment frames household conditions; the Powering the Economy Act links to 45 tracked projects.
provinces.marketContext: Nova Scotia's tracked pipeline spans 339 projects with ~$13B in stated value. The largest component is power/energy (8 valued projects, ~$8.9B), led by the $8B Bear Head Energy project. Offshore wind (first call up to 5 GW, Wind West $60B framework) and natural-gas power generation tie the pipeline to electricity and gas markets; >50 companies are active in supply-chain sectors.
provinces.tradeExposure: Nova Scotia exposure runs through offshore wind and gas power: 8 valued power/energy projects (~$8.9B) led by Bear Head Energy ($8B), within a Wind West $60B / 5 GW framework.

provinces.name: New Brunswick
provinces.analysis:
New Brunswick unemployment was 7.2% in April 2026, above the national 6.9%; the April LFS showed employment -2,700 (-0.7%)4. New Brunswick CPI was +1.0% year-over-year, the lowest provincial CPI, and provincial GDP growth registered +1.8%.

New Brunswick launched an economic development strategy targeting 10% economic growth by 2030 across critical minerals, trade corridors and ports, energy capacity, and interprovincial trade1. The 2026-27 budget, tabled March 17, carries no new taxes and a CA$1.39B deficit, with Opportunities NB offering up to $54.3M over three years for company modernization2.

The provincial energy plan targets +600 MW of SMR capacity at Point Lepreau by 2035, +1,400 MW of wind, and +500 MW of solar3. The project database tracks 198 New Brunswick projects with roughly $7.1B in stated value: ports and logistics leads with 4 valued projects (~$1.9B), infrastructure adds 29 projects (~$1.8B), and forestry adds 3 projects (~$1.2B) including the $1.1B Saint John Pulp Mill Upgrades. Lumber and pulp prices flow through to the forestry pipeline.
provinces.sectorHighlights: Ports and logistics leads New Brunswick's tracked pipeline with 4 valued projects (~$1.9B), including the $0.96B Small Craft Harbours renewal and the $0.21B Port Saint John West Side terminals modernization. Infrastructure adds 29 projects (~$1.8B) and forestry 3 projects (~$1.2B), led by the $1.1B Saint John Pulp Mill Upgrades. The energy plan adds SMR, wind and solar capacity upstream of future capital.
provinces.labourDeepDive: New Brunswick unemployment was 7.2% in April 2026, above the national 6.9%; the April LFS showed employment -2,700 (-0.7%). Participation rate was 60.6% and the employment rate 56.3%. The economic-development strategy targets a 16.8% increase in private-sector capital investment by 2030, with Opportunities NB funding up to $54.3M over three years.
provinces.consumerPulse: New Brunswick CPI was +1.0% year-over-year, the lowest provincial CPI, while provincial GDP growth registered +1.8%. Unemployment at 7.2% is above the national 6.9%. The 2026-27 budget carries no new taxes and a CA$1.39B deficit, framing the household and fiscal backdrop.
provinces.marketContext: New Brunswick's tracked pipeline spans 198 projects with ~$7.1B in stated value. Largest components are Ports & Logistics (4 valued projects, ~$1.9B), infrastructure (29 projects, ~$1.8B), and forestry (3 projects, ~$1.2B). Lumber/pulp prices flow through to the Saint John Pulp Mill Upgrades ($1.1B); the energy plan adds SMR, wind and solar capacity upstream of future capital.

provinces.name: Newfoundland and Labrador
provinces.analysis:
Newfoundland and Labrador unemployment was 10.0% in April 20264, the highest among provinces, and the employment rate 51.6%, the lowest. The April LFS showed employment -5,200 (-2.1%), the largest single-month percentage decline among provinces. Provincial GDP growth registered +2.4% and CPI +2.3% year-over-year.

Equinor submitted the Bay du Nord development application to the provincial energy regulator in early May 20261; the March 2026 provincial agreement provides up to $6.4B in direct provincial revenue in phase one, with project investment around $14B and first oil targeted around 20312. Offshore oil and gas sustains roughly 20,000 jobs, about 20% of provincial GDP and 55% of exports.

The project database tracks 1,561 Newfoundland and Labrador projects with roughly $25.8B in stated value: power and energy leads with 7 valued projects (~$16.5B), anchored by Grassy Point LNG ($10B) and the White Rose Expansion ($3.8B + $2.3B), and mining adds 9 projects (~$6.1B) including the $3.86B Kami iron-ore project. Brent and WTI price moves flow directly through to the offshore base; the Bay du Nord application sits upstream of future activity.

Mining follows with 9 projects (~$6.1B), including the $3.86B Kami iron-ore project and the $0.53B Valentine gold mine. The Bay du Nord application (~$14B investment) sits upstream of future offshore activity.

provinces.name: Prince Edward Island
provinces.analysis:
Prince Edward Island unemployment was 8.0% in April 20263 and CPI +4.0% year-over-year, the highest provincial CPI. Provincial GDP growth registered +3.6%, the highest provincial GDP growth.

The 2026 budget, tabled April 14, sets a five-year capital plan totaling $1.6B; the FY2026/27 deficit is pegged at $409.9M (roughly 3.5% of GDP), with a new personal income tax bracket above $200,0001. Nominal GDP is assumed at +4% for 2026/2027 and real GDP at +2%, down from roughly 2.4% in 2025; the budget centers on health care, affordability and energy security2.

The project database tracks 82 PEI projects with roughly $1.5B in stated value, the smallest provincial pipeline. Power and energy leads with 13 valued projects (~$0.6B), covering wind and submarine transmission, and infrastructure adds 39 projects (~$0.5B) of provincial roads and bridges. Wind capacity ties the pipeline to electricity-system planning; the 39-project infrastructure set aligns with the provincial capital plan.
provinces.sectorHighlights: Power and energy leads PEI's tracked pipeline with 13 valued projects (~$0.6B), covering wind and submarine transmission, including the $0.09B Northumberland Strait submarine transmission system, the $0.09B Skinners Pond wind centre, and the $0.07B Summerside solar and storage integration. Infrastructure adds 39 projects (~$0.5B) of provincial roads and bridges, aligned with the $1.6B five-year capital plan.

provinces.consumerPulse: PEI CPI was +4.0% year-over-year, the highest provincial CPI, while provincial GDP growth registered +3.6%, the highest provincial GDP growth. Unemployment was 8.0%. The 2026-27 budget centers on health care, affordability and energy security and introduces a new personal income tax bracket above $200,000.
provinces.marketContext: Prince Edward Island's tracked pipeline spans 82 projects with ~$1.5B in stated value, the smallest provincial pipeline. Largest components are power/energy (13 valued projects, ~$0.6B; wind and submarine transmission) and infrastructure (39 projects, ~$0.5B; provincial roads and bridges). Wind capacity ties the pipeline to electricity-system planning; direct commodity exposure is limited given project scale.
provinces.tradeExposure: Prince Edward Island's pipeline is small (~$1.5B) and led by power/energy (13 projects, ~$0.6B; wind and submarine transmission) and provincial road/bridge infrastructure; direct commodity exposure is limited given project scale.

provinces.name: Yukon
provinces.analysis:
Yukon unemployment was 5.3% in April 2026 with an employment rate of 71.2%, the highest among all jurisdictions1. Territorial GDP was -3.3% for 2024, the latest available; Statistics Canada does not publish CPI or housing starts for the territories.

Yukon tabled a $2.46B 2026-27 budget ($2.07B operations, $385M capital) with an $81.8M deficit; capital spending falls as the Nisutlin Bay Bridge replacement and the Whitehorse airport runway project wind down2. The Canada-Yukon Workforce Tariff Response provides $1.5M over three years for tariff-affected construction, transportation and mining workers and employers3.

The project database tracks 123 Yukon projects with roughly $46.4B in stated value, dominated by a single proposed $40B Northern Defence and Infrastructure Investment. Mining adds 4 valued projects (~$4.6B), including the $3.62B Casino copper-gold project, tying part of the pipeline to copper and placer-gold prices. The remaining 54 infrastructure projects (~$1.0B) reflect winding-down territorial capital.

Mining adds 4 valued projects (~$4.6B), including the $3.62B Casino copper-gold project and the $0.49B Kudz Ze Kayah base-metals project. Infrastructure covers 54 projects (~$1.0B), including the $0.36B Yukon Resource Gateway roads, reflecting winding-down territorial capital.

provinces.name: Northwest Territories
provinces.analysis:
Northwest Territories unemployment was 6.8% in April 2026 with an employment rate of 66.1%3. Territorial GDP was -1.1% for 2024, the latest available; Statistics Canada does not publish CPI or housing starts for the territories.

The NWT diamond industry is contracting: Rio Tinto plans to close Diavik in March 2026 as reserves are exhausted, while Gahcho Kue continues to 20311. The three operating mines directly and indirectly employ over 1,500 residents and account for roughly one-fifth of NWT GDP. The GNWT released a geological assessment of 1,721 mineral showings across 19 critical minerals, including lithium, cobalt, copper and zinc, as a diversification path, with commercial attractiveness contingent on higher prices2.

The project database tracks 182 NWT projects with roughly $40.1B in stated value, dominated by a single proposed $35B Arctic Defence and Infrastructure Spending Package. Mining adds 5 valued projects (~$2.0B), including the $0.65B Pine Point lead-zinc project and the $0.59B NICO cobalt-gold-bismuth mine; the $1.20B Taltson hydro expansion anchors power and energy.

Power and energy is anchored by the $1.20B Taltson hydroelectric expansion. The Diavik closure removes part of a diamond sector worth roughly one-fifth of NWT GDP.

provinces.name: Nunavut
provinces.analysis:
Nunavut unemployment was 12.0% in April 20263, the highest among all jurisdictions, with an employment rate of 55.0%, the lowest. Territorial GDP was +7.5% for 2024, the latest available; Statistics Canada does not publish CPI or housing starts for the territories.

The Prime Minister referred the Grays Bay Road and Port project, a deepwater export terminal plus airstrip with dual-use civilian and military scope, to the Major Projects Office on March 12, 20261. CanNor announced over $13M for four Nunavut projects in April 20262, including $4.5M to West Kitikmeot Resources for Grays Bay environmental and feasibility studies and $1.1M for an Iqaluit economic-development hub; Canada-Nunavut joint funding of $2.45M supports Baffin Island critical-mineral research.

The project database tracks 47 Nunavut projects with roughly $2B in stated value, the smallest jurisdictional pipeline. The only valued mining record is B2Gold's Back River Gold project ($0.61B); infrastructure adds 13 projects (~$0.6B) covering water, power and waste facilities. Gold prices intersect Back River Gold; the Grays Bay referral sits upstream of future critical-mineral export capacity.
